events.title: Q4 2025 Allient Inc Earnings Call
events.transcript:
Craig Mychajluk
Vice President of Finance and Investor Relations, Alliance Advisors IR
Thank you, and good morning, everyone. We appreciate your time and interest in Allient. On the call today are Dick Warzala, our Chairman, President, and CEO, and Jim Michaud, our Chief Financial Officer. Dick and Jim will review our Q4 and full year 2025 results, provide a strategic and operational update, and share our outlook. We will open the line for questions. The earnings release and slide presentation are available on our website at allient.com. If you are following along, please turn to slide 2 for the safe harbor statement. Forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those indicated. These risks and factors are outlined in our SEC filings and the earnings release.
We will also discuss certain non-GAAP measures useful in evaluating performance. These measures should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP results. Reconciliations of non-GAAP to GAAP measures are provided in the tables accompanying the earnings release and slides. Please turn to slide 3. I now turn the call over to Dick.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Craig. Welcome everyone. We entered 2025 with clear priorities: expanding structural margins, strengthening the balance sheet, and positioning the portfolio around durable secular growth drivers. As the year closes, we made measurable progress on all three. Q4 highlights include improving industrial demand, disciplined execution, and structural margin expansion driven by our Simplify to Accelerate NOW program. This performance reflects higher volumes, operating leverage, improved mix, and sustained cost discipline, translating into stronger profitability. Broad participation across industrial verticals reinforced diversification and durability of results.
A significant automation destocking is largely behind us, and ordering patterns are returning to normalized levels. Demand for power quality solutions supporting data center infrastructure remains strong. Vehicle performance exceeded expectations due to commercial auto production timing. Medical remained steady, and aerospace and defense reflected normal program timing dynamics. Q4 results showed broad participation across the portfolio. Margin expansion was not solely volume-driven.
Margin improvement reflected better mix, improved cost structure, and continued execution under Simplify to Accelerate NOW. Operational work from prior years is now embedded in the model. For the full year, 2025 focused on strengthening the company foundation: reducing complexity, improving throughput, and strengthening margins sustainably. Structural savings of $6–7 million were targeted, with meaningful progress realized through footprint optimization and resource focus.
Product development was accelerated by streamlining processes and reducing time to market. Lean manufacturing improved standard work and reduced non-value-added time. The Dothan facility transitioned to advanced fabrication, with assembly work moved to complementary sites. This initiative is expected to reduce costs and complexity across North America. Record gross margins were achieved, and operating income grew ahead of revenue.
We generated record operating cash flow. We reduced net debt significantly, bringing leverage down to levels that gives us real financial flexibility. The balance sheet today looks very different than it did a year ago, and that matters because it allows us to invest in organic growth, support new program launches, and pursue disciplined capital allocation opportunities from a position of strength. With that, let me turn it over to Jim for a more in-depth review of the financials.
Jim Michaud
CFO, Allient Inc
Record operating cash flow was generated. Net debt was reduced significantly, providing financial flexibility. The balance sheet allows investment in organic growth, support for new programs, and disciplined capital allocation. I now turn the call to Jim for an in-depth review of the financials.
Demand for power quality solutions supporting data center infrastructure remained strong. Vehicle revenue increased 35% due to increased commercial automotive shipments tied to a transitioning model program. Construction markets improved, and powersports conditions stabilized. Medical revenue increased 9%, supported by steady demand for surgical instruments and precise motion applications. Aerospace and defense declined 5%, reflecting the lumpy nature of shipments and the previously announced M10 Booker tank program cancellation. Underlying defense program activity remains solid. Distribution channel sales increased 11%, a smaller component of total revenue. Turning to slide 6.
This slide shows revenue composition over the trailing twelve months, year-over-year changes, and key drivers. Industrial remains our largest vertical, anchored by higher-value applications. Power quality for data centers, motion solutions tied to automation, and applications aligned with electrification are where engineering focus and capital have been directed. Aerospace and Defense remains a meaningful and growing contributor. While quarterly shipments can be lumpy, underlying program activity and pipeline remain solid, providing longer cycle visibility. Medical remains steady. Surgical applications continue to be reliable contributors, and precision motion capabilities position us well in this space.
Vehicle is now a smaller percentage of the mix than previously, partly market-driven and partly strategic. We have intentionally shifted from lower-margin programs toward higher-value applications across the portfolio. Today’s mix is more margin accretive and better aligned with durable secular growth drivers. On slide 7, gross margin expanded 90 basis points year-over-year to 32.4%, driven by higher volumes, favorable mix, and operational efficiencies from Simplify to Accelerate NOW. Sequentially, gross margin moderated due to a higher proportion of vehicle revenue, which carries lower relative margins.
For the full year, gross margin expanded 150 basis points to a record 32.8%. Slide 8 highlights drivers behind margin and operating income expansion. The Simplify to Accelerate NOW program was designed to structurally reduce complexity, improve throughput, and strengthen margins. Operating performance reflects this work. Structural savings from 2024 and 2025 are embedded in the business, showing up in leverage and operating income expansion. Realignment costs relate primarily to the Dolphin transition, which has been successful operationally and financially.
Enhanced manufacturing focus and early savings elements are being realized. Combined with improved volume and mix, leverage impact is clear. Expense discipline improved at the operating level. Higher volumes were captured while controlling SG&A, allowing operating income to grow faster than revenue. Q4 operating income increased 76% to $11.4 million (7.9% of revenue). Full-year operating income increased 46% to $44 million (7.9% of revenue). Slide 9 illustrates how structural margin expansion and disciplined execution translated into bottom-line growth. Net income for the quarter more than doubled to $6.4 million ($0.38 per diluted share).
Adjusted net income was $9.3 million ($0.55 per share). Adjusted EBITDA was $19 million (13.3% of revenue), up 170 basis points. Full-year net income was $22 million ($1.32 per diluted share). Adjusted EBITDA was $76.9 million (13.9% of revenue), representing a 210 basis point expansion year-over-year. Full-year effective tax rate was 23.3%. For 2026, expected tax rate is 21–23%. Slide 10 reflects execution against three financial priorities: improving working capital and inventory efficiency, reducing structural costs, and strengthening the balance sheet.
Cash generation reached record operating cash flow of $56.7 million, up 35% year-over-year, reflecting improved profitability and working capital management. Inventory discipline was a major focus in 2025. Automation normalization and rare earth considerations were navigated while improving inventory turns to 3.2 times versus 2.7 at end of 2024. Planning processes were tightened, production aligned with demand, and excess inventory reduced while maintaining strong customer service levels. Receivables day sales outstanding improved to 57 days versus 60 last year, reflecting better collections, stronger billing discipline, and improved customer mix.
Combined inventory turns improvement with DSO reduction demonstrates a structurally better working capital profile. Capital expenditures in 2025 were $7 million, focused on customer programs and productivity initiatives. For 2026, CapEx is expected at $10–12 million, supporting customer programs and growth initiatives. Slide 10 highlights execution: working capital improvement achieved, structural cost reductions realized, and debt re-reduction accomplished. Total debt declined to $180.4 million.
Net debt declined to $139.7 million, a $48.4 million reduction year-over-year. Leverage ratio improved to 1.82x from 3.01 at end of 2024. Bank-defined leverage ratio ended at 2.34, comfortably within covenant levels. Stronger earnings, improved cash conversion, and disciplined CapEx enabled material deleveraging. Benefits include lower financial risk and reduced interest burden, and increased flexibility to invest in organic growth, support new programs, and pursue disciplined capital deployment. Slides 10 and 11 together illustrate operational improvements translating into cash, deleveraging, and flexibility.
That completes the financial overview for Q4. Please advance to Slide 12. I will now turn the call back over to Dick.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Jim. As we moved through Q4, order trends improved. Automation demand is stabilizing, power quality for data center infrastructure remains strong, and our aerospace and defense pipeline continues to provide long-term cycle visibility. Orders were up sequentially and year-over-year, with a book-to-bill ratio slightly above 1. Backlog ended the year at approximately $233 million, with most expected to convert within 3 to 9 months, consistent with historical patterns. This visibility supports a constructive start to 2026. We are positioned to build on momentum while remaining realistic, as the macro environment is uneven across certain end markets.26, we believe we are positioned to build on that momentum. At the same time, we remain realistic. The macro environment is still uneven across certain end markets.
Customer capital spending can move in phases. Policy and tariff considerations remain part of the broader landscape, and we continue to monitor developments closely. We will adjust as needed. Regarding recent Supreme Court rulings and trade policy discussions, we continue to evaluate potential implications. Over the past several years, we have diversified our supply base, localized sourcing where appropriate, and managed tariff exposure through pricing and operational adjustments. We remain disciplined in evaluating these developments. What gives us confidence is what we control: our cost structure, which is structurally stronger than a few years ago, and working capital discipline demonstrated in 2025.
We control capital allocation and strengthened the balance sheet meaningfully over the past year. We continue to align the portfolio around higher-value motion controls and power solutions, serving durable secular drivers of electrification, automation, energy efficiency, increased defense spending, and digital infrastructure. These drivers are long-term shifts in how energy is generated and used, systems are automated, and infrastructure is built. Allient technologies are directly aligned with these transitions. We exit 2025 with improved margins, stronger cash flow, and a materially stronger balance sheet, providing flexibility and resilience and positioning us to execute through varying market conditions. We believe we will enter 2026 from a position of strength.
We have an excellent opportunity to leverage the foundation built through our Simplify to Accelerate NOW initiatives, simplify the organization, drive out cost, and accelerate growth well into the future. Operator, please open the line for questions.
Operator
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star, then one on a touch-tone phone. For speakerphone users, pick up your handset before pressing the keys. To withdraw a question, press star then two. Our first question comes from Tomohiko Sano with J.P. Morgan. Please go ahead.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Hi, good morning, everyone.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Good morning, Tomo.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Thank you for taking my questions. While the cyclical macro recovery, such as improving ISM, is expected, Allient has clearly driven structural growth and margin improvement through initiatives like Simplify to Accelerate NOW. Looking ahead to 2026, which do you see as the bigger contributor to growth and margin expansion: external tailwinds or your own initiatives, such as self-help measures? Any additional color on 2026, please.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Okay. If I understand correctly, you are asking which secular drivers we expect to generate the largest growth opportunities for 2026. Is that correct?
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
I want more insight into the cyclical recovery versus the 2026 secular themes.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Tomo, I’m having a hard time picking up some of the comments—your line is breaking up.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
I meant, could you discuss 2026 revenue growth driven by cyclical recovery versus structural items? I also want some color on the margin side. Thank you.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Okay, I understand now. As we reposition the business, we see longer-term drivers continuing. Data center infrastructure remains a key opportunity. On the energy side, some companies are generating power independently, which does not affect us.
We play a significant role in ensuring power is delivered efficiently and effectively as data centers expand. This opportunity continues into 2026 and beyond, based on infrastructure and capital projects, subject to prime contractors and developers’ timing. Aerospace and defense, particularly defense, is influenced by many factors.
The ongoing conflict in Iran may impact our business, immediately or long-term—it is too soon to call. Other active programs, including defense applications like drones and missile defense, continue to see our participation and are expected to persist.
North American-based manufacturing and design engineering provides us an advantage for defense products. Medical remains a growth area, particularly with AI and advanced diagnostic tools. Key areas where we have long-term involvement continue to expand.
Industrial automation and robotics, including humanoids, continue to be areas of participation and growth. Germany’s industrial markets remain soft, with no projected growth for 2026. We will monitor developments, but that is the current forecast.
We saw some signs that the market might improve, but the latest information suggests otherwise. Our diversification across multiple markets provides balance. The industrial sector is expected to continue growing due to automation and data center infrastructure. Defense growth is also anticipated, influenced by cycle timing, as Jim mentioned.
The government canceled the M10 Booker program, reflecting a realignment of priorities on the battlefield. Margins are influenced significantly by product mix. Our focus remains on investing in markets with margins above our average, and capital spending will align with this strategy. This disciplined approach positions us well for the year.
Our book-to-bill ratio is improving, which we monitor closely to confirm that opportunities are converting into shipments. This demonstrates that our pipeline is being realized effectively. I hope this answers your questions; if not, I am happy to provide further clarification.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Thank you. Very helpful. A follow-up on capital allocation: congratulations on improved leverage and strong cash flow. How do you plan to prioritize capital allocation for 2026 among organic growth, investments, M&A, and shareholder returns?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Going into 2026, our pipeline of opportunities is strong. Investments will focus on areas under our control and immediate opportunities that require funding to realize. This will represent the majority of our capital allocation. We are also monitoring potential acquisition opportunities and are positioned to act if the right opportunities arise.
Regarding Simplify to Accelerate NOW, the initiative is ongoing. Several initiatives were successfully executed, but some actions carried into 2026. We will continue to drive cost reductions and efficiency improvements across our infrastructure and footprint. This is a continuing process.
This is not a short-term effort. There remain additional opportunities in 2026 to improve our cost base. We will actively pursue these initiatives to enhance efficiency and drive value.
Tomohiko Sano
Research Analyst, J.P. Morgan
Thank you, very helpful. That’s all from me.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Tomo.
Operator
The next question comes from Greg Palm with Craig-Hallum. Please go ahead.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Thanks. Morning, everybody. Congrats on a strong finish to 2025.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Greg.
David Brown
Equity Research Analyst, Robert W. Baird & Co.
Appreciate it, Greg.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
I don’t remember the last time you grew revenues sequentially from Q3 to Q4. Maybe it happened once or twice. Was this due to growth in commercial vehicles, or were there other factors? Also, what trends have you seen so far in Q1?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Great question. Q4 is always subject to unknowns. Some demand was pent-up, and supply chain factors caused irregularities in normal cyclical patterns. We experienced a few pull-ins, which elevated Q4 sales. The commercial vehicle side contributed, but other areas also had minor surprises. Some demand shifted, which may reduce Q1 activity, but these are expected offsets.
You know, that was a one-time surge based upon some demand that was sitting out there, and we see it, you know, returning to normal. In a couple other areas, there were a few that surprises, I'll call them, and I won't mention in detail what they were. They were, you know, pulling in product, then as we turned the year, we saw that that was reflected in a little bit lower demand in Q1. There were some offsets there that, you know, we'll be addressing and see as it's still early, of course, but see how that lands.
Overall, three drivers affected Q4: a one-time surge returning to normal and two adjustments after pulled-in demand. Nothing seen will affect annual run rates; it was an unusual quarter.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Across your markets, what is the current demand trend? Any changes or potential risks and opportunities over the past week?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Order inputs are strong, showing continued improvement through the year. We monitor this closely as it indicates future shipments. Encouragingly, the trend appears to be continuing.
Recently, defense product consumption exceeded expectations, indicating a stockpile was being drawn down. Shipments are now resuming, particularly for replenishment of defense-related products. The exact impact is uncertain, but we anticipate seeing results soon.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
You mentioned drones as an opportunity. Can you share any traction or emerging opportunities there?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
We are well-regarded for high-performance solutions and custom engineering. Activity in the drone market has accelerated, including prototyping and quoting. Opportunities are expanding into Class 1/Group 1 devices. This area is a key growth opportunity, and we know how to scale production in volume.
We benefit from maintaining automotive as a single-digit percentage of our business. This allows us to produce higher-volume solutions cost-competitively using automation. I see this as a strong opportunity to redeploy the know-how we have developed over the years into new growth areas.
While pricing and margins may differ from our higher-performance custom-engineered products, volume provides incremental margin contributions. The shift to North America has increased inquiries. Our technology base—electronics, controls, motors, lightweighting, and composites—positions us to expand in these areas, and we are excited about the opportunity.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Last question: you announced a facility expansion for data center work last year. What is the status? Will you have adequate capacity to capitalize on growth opportunities?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
The expansion is progressing well and is expected to be fully operational by late Q2 or early Q3. Timing couldn’t be better. This proactive increase in footprint and capabilities positions us to meet growing market demand, with significant volume increases expected later in the year.
Greg Palm
Senior Research Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group
Perfect. Appreciate all the color. Thanks.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Greg.
Operator
The next question comes from Max Michaelis with Lake Street Capital Markets. Please go ahead.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
Thanks. Regarding the data center opportunity, based on your prepared remarks and Q&A, can we expect acceleration in growth in 2026 compared to 2025?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Yes. Opportunities are strong. The facility expansion at our main site, nearing completion, is critical to handling increased demand. Last year saw some accelerated deliveries. Order input rates are variable, so growth will not be a smooth incremental trend.
Expect substantial jumps in Q3 and Q4 as orders and shipments ramp. The trajectory will not be linear.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
Is growth driven primarily by new customer wins or expanding wallet share with existing customers?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
The market itself is expanding. Our capabilities position us competitively, driving growth. Past acquisitions, including a Wisconsin facility and manufacturing footprint in Mexico, have accelerated our ability to meet demand and support market expansion.
We are leveraging our production capabilities, facility expansions, and technology to strengthen our competitive edge. Our products are recognized as high-performing and cost-effective.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
With the M10 Booker program ending, are there other programs you can discuss for future direction?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
I prefer not to share specifics. The M10 Booker program was a multi-year effort. Battlefield priorities are shifting toward smaller, agile, autonomous vehicles. We are positioned well in these emerging areas.
Through acquisitions, we offer fully integrated solutions, including electrification, actuation, motors, controls, drives, IO, and lightweight composites. Composites improve strength, EMI protection, and efficiency in electric and hybrid vehicles, extending battery life.
We are uniquely positioned to offer these solutions to prime contractors. The Department of Defense is emphasizing accelerated development. Leveraging products already used in other markets gives us a competitive advantage, particularly in vehicle applications where we are strong.
COTS (commercial off-the-shelf) products are critical. We can modify them for ruggedness, environmental factors, lighter weight, or higher performance. Investments have been made, and while returns are pending, we are confident in our positioning for the future.
Max Michaelis
Equity Research Associate Analyst, Lake Street Capital Markets
Awesome. Thanks.
Jim Michaud
CFO, Allient Inc
If you have a question, please press star then 1. Our next question comes from Ted Jackson with Northland Securities. Please go ahead.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Thanks very much. You guys sound so optimistic—it’s infectious.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Ted.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
I have a couple of questions. Dick, regarding the domestication of work: there are two main areas—manufacturing and supply chain. Manufacturing seems straightforward. For supply chain, is there work required to ensure NDAA compliance by January?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Good question. There’s always work to be done, particularly with rare earth minerals and materials in higher-performing products. We have the capacity to produce in North America, with about 1.2 million square feet of manufacturing space. Facility rationalization over the past years gives us a redeployable footprint, which is to our advantage.
We have space for quick ramp-ups for certain initiatives. Supply chain remains a challenge; we are actively working on it. While not fully solved, we are addressing government policies and other external factors.
We are minimizing impacts and solidifying supply chain sources. Ramp-up hasn’t been as fast as desired, and alignment between government objectives and reality will take time. We are proactively regionalizing our supply chain.
These efforts are independent of tariffs or duties—they were logical business decisions. We remain prepared but cannot control all external factors. Jim, anything to add?
Jim Michaud
CFO, Allient Inc
Ted, federal investments in US companies are ongoing. Supply chain compliance, including rare earths, will evolve and likely won’t be fully resolved by January 1.
We have teams working diligently with suppliers to lay the foundation for partnerships aligned with government investments.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Regarding magnets, everyone has that challenge. Does the government understand practical limitations? Are you in dialogue with them?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Yes. We are in close contact with government officials and identified sources being supported. Reality and desire must align. We remain fully engaged and committed.
It’s a continuous effort to work all angles while staying close to key government activities.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Beyond magnets, are there other critical components that require resourcing for compliance?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Yes, but they are less complicated. Costs are a factor. Some electronic components face supply shortages due to demand in other sectors. For motors, alternatives exist for laminated steel and bearings, though they may be costlier.
Magnets are unique and deserve attention. Other components are impacted by external factors but are manageable.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
This will remain a discussion topic each quarter. On commercial vehicles in Q4, can you quantify the one-time impact to help frame Q1 expectations?
Q4 seasonality to Q1 is typical. Commercial vehicle market seems to be rebounding, with freight rates and Class 8 orders picking up from November through February.
This improvement should translate to stronger demand in H2 2026, setting up well for 2027. What is Allient supplying into this market, and how do you see it evolving?
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Are you asking about commercial automotive specifically or all vehicles?
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Yeah
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Truck and construction, or all of them?
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
All of them. I’m interested in the full picture.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
We saw improvements across commercial automotive, bus, construction, marine, agricultural, truck, rail, and Power Sports. Vehicle business remains a single-digit percentage. We define “vehicle” broadly to include all these sectors.
Vehicle markets have long design cycles, are cost competitive, and capital intensive. Investments are focused elsewhere. Power Sports has grown automotive-like. One-time Q4 impact is about $2.5 million.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
Okay.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
In Q4, across agricultural, construction, and other vehicles, we supply actuators and steering applications—gas, petrol, or electrified. We also provide electrohydraulics in larger vehicles. Expertise focuses on steering, extending to industrial applications as well.
Ted Jackson
Managing Director, Senior Equity Research Analyst, Northland Securities
That helps. Thanks.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you, Ted. Operator, are there any more questions?
Operator
This concludes the Q&A. Returning the conference to management for closing remarks.
Richard Warzala
Chairman, President, and CEO, Allient Inc
Thank you for joining today. We will participate in the J.P. Morgan Industrials Conference in Washington, DC, on 17 March. Please reach out anytime. We look forward to speaking after Q1 2026 results. Have a great day—this concludes the call.
Operator
The conference is now concluded. Thank you for attending.

events.transcript:
Operator
Good morning, and welcome to the Allient Inc. Second Quarter Fiscal Year 2025 Financial Results Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please note, this event is being recorded.
I would now like to turn the conference over to Craig Mychajluk, Investor Relations. Please go ahead.
Craig Mychajluk
Senior Vice President of Operations
Yes. Thank you, and good morning, everyone. We certainly appreciate your time today as well as your interest in Allient.
Joining me today are Dick Warzala, our Chairman, President and CEO; and Jim Michaud, our Chief Financial Officer. Dick and Jim will walk through our second quarter 2025 results, provide a strategic update and share our outlook. We'll then open up the call for Q&A. You should have a copy of the financial results that were released yesterday after the market closed. If not, you can find it on our website at allient.com, along with the slides that accompany today's discussion.
If you're reviewing those slides, please turn to Slide 2 for the safe harbor statement. As you are aware, we may make forward-looking statements on this call during the formal discussion as well as during the Q&A. These statements apply to future events that are subject to risks and uncertainties as well as other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from what is stated on today's call. These risks and uncertainties and other factors are discussed in the earnings release as well as with other documents filed by the company with the Securities and Exchange Commission. You can find these documents on our website or at sec.gov.
I want to point out as well that during today's call, we will discuss some non-GAAP measures, which we believe will be useful in evaluating our performance. You should not consider the presentation of this additional information in isolation or as a substitute for results prepared in accordance with GAAP. We have provided reconciliations of non-GAAP to comparable GAAP measures in the tables accompanying the earnings release as well as the slides.
So with that, please turn to Slide 3, and I'll turn it over to Dick to begin. Dick?
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Thank you, Craig, and welcome, everyone. We continue to build momentum in the second quarter, delivering record gross margin, strong profitability and exceptional cash generation. This performance reflects the consistent execution of our operational priorities and the alignment we are seeing across our markets, organization and strategic road map.
Revenue increased 5% sequentially and 3% year-over-year, supported by solid demand in data center infrastructure, defense and select high-value medical applications. While powersports within the vehicle market remained under pressure, we did see healthy sequential growth from that vertical. It is worth noting that approximately $3 million to $4 million of revenue was pulled into the second quarter as customers accelerated shipments due to concerns around supply constraints in heavy rare earth materials.
Gross margin reached a record 33.2%, up 100 basis points sequentially and 330 basis points from a year ago, driven by a favorable mix, higher volumes and continued improvement in operating discipline. This translated into meaningful EBITDA growth and a significant increase in profitability with net income up 58% from Q1 and nearly fivefold year-over-year.
We also generated $24.5 million in operating cash during the quarter, another record, which enabled us to further reduce debt and strengthen our balance sheet. Our Simplify to Accelerate NOW program remains central to our performance, driving efficiency, aligning with evolving customer needs and enhancing responsiveness across our global operations.
The operational foundation we have built is delivering results even in a dynamic external environment, including tariff and material supply challenges, particularly in heavy rare earths, where we are actively managing constraints. The initiatives we put in place are tracking well, both in terms of cost savings and operational agility. For example, our [ goals in ] restructuring launched as a cornerstone of the 2025 effort is on track and expected to play a meaningful role in achieving the $6 million to $7 million in targeted annualized savings this year.
Looking ahead, we remain focused on building on this momentum, executing with discipline, scaling the benefits of our transformation initiatives and advancing toward our long-term financial and strategic objectives.
With that, let me turn it over to Jim for a more in-depth review of the financials.
James A. Michaud
Senior VP & Chief Financial Officer
Thank you, Dick, and good morning, everyone. Let's begin with Slide 5. Revenue for the second quarter was $139.6 million, a 3% increase year-over-year and up 5% sequentially. This growth was driven by continued strength in our aerospace and defense programs, industrial markets, especially HVAC and data center infrastructure and select medical applications. Revenue growth also benefited from a favorable foreign exchange impact of $2.4 million.
Sales to U.S. customers accounted for 55% of total revenue, in line with last year. The geographic and end market diversification of our portfolio remains a key strength. Looking at our market performance, Aerospace and Defense grew 13%, reflecting program timing and strong execution. We continue to see a healthy pipeline of opportunities in the defense sector and believe this market will remain a solid contributor to growth as we move forward.
Medical was up 4%, led by solid demand for surgical instruments. The industrial market increased 3%, driven by continued strength for HVAC and data center market applications where our power quality solutions are needed. We are also encouraged by early signs of recovery in industrial automation, where demand has been challenged over the past year given the inventory destocking. We are beginning to see more consistent activity and ordering trends. Vehicle revenue was down 7% due to ongoing softness in powersports, although we did see sequential sales improvement in the vehicle market.
Now turning to Slide 6 for the composition of our revenue over the trailing 12 months, along with the key catalysts driving these changes. We have seen a meaningful shift in mix with growth in higher value industrial and aerospace defense solutions helping to offset ongoing pressure in the vehicle market. This evolution reflects not only external market dynamics such as softness in recreational spend and volatility in automation, but also our deliberate effort to focus on more resilient margin-accretive applications.
The industrial sector is our largest market and reflects similar impacts as the recent quarter. Aerospace and defense continues to be a growth driver. Meanwhile, our vehicle exposure has been intentionally refined. While near-term demand in powersports remains soft, our proactive repositioning away from lower-margin programs is helping to protect profitability. Overall, our revenue mix today is more diversified, more balanced and better aligned with where we see long-term opportunity, and that puts us in a strong position to manage near-term headwinds while driving sustained performance.
On Slide 7, we are pleased to report a record gross margin of 33.2%, up 330 basis points from last year and 100 basis points sequentially. This improvement marks our fourth consecutive quarter of expansion. Key drivers included favorable mix, higher volumes and ongoing implementation of lean manufacturing disciplines as well as our Simplify to Accelerate NOW program.
Slide 8 highlights our operating leverage. Operating income more than doubled to $11.7 million with operating margin rising 480 basis points year-over-year to 8.4% and improving 180 basis points sequentially. SG&A was 14.7% of sales, down 60 basis points from last year, demonstrating cost discipline despite inflationary and incentive-based pressures. Restructuring and business realignment costs were $1.1 million in the quarter, supporting future margin improvement.
Turning to Slide 9. Net income increased to $5.6 million or $0.34 per diluted share. On an adjusted basis, net income was $9.5 million or $0.57 per diluted share, up from $0.46 per share in Q1 and $0.29 per share in the prior year. Our effective tax rate for Q2 was 23.1% as we continue to expect our full rate to land between 21% and 23%. As for interest expense, we did see an increase despite lower debt levels. As we discussed last quarter, this was largely due to the expiration of 2 favorable interest rate swaps late last year, which were replaced at higher prevailing rates. While still competitive in today's market, they are not as favorable as the prior arrangements.
Additionally, our amended credit facility carries a modestly higher spread contributing to the increase. That said, our overall interest burden remains manageable, and our strong cash flow is enabling continuing deleveraging. Adjusted EBITDA increased meaningful to $20.1 million or 14.4% of revenue, driving strong conversion on higher volumes and a more favorable mix. This represents margin expansion of 420 basis points year-over-year and 120 basis points sequentially.
Turning to Slide 10. We delivered record operating cash flow of $24.5 million in the quarter, up 76% sequentially and nearly 3x the level generated in the same period last year. On a year-to-date basis, operating cash flow now stands at $38.4 million, more than double what we achieved in the first half of 2024. This strong performance reflects both profit growth and disciplined working capital execution.
Our inventory turns improved to 3.1x, up from 2.7x at the end of the year. This was driven by tighter demand alignment, better planning and continued progress under our Simplify to Accelerate NOW initiative. At the same time, our days sales outstanding improved, signaling stronger collections and more efficient conversion of sales into cash. We used a portion of our cash to reduce debt by $20 million in the quarter, bringing us to the balance sheet discussion on Slide 11.
We ended Q2 with nearly $50 million in cash and lowered our net debt by $35.8 million year-to-date, bringing our leverage ratio down to 2.3x compared with 3x at the end of last year. Our bank-defined leverage ratio, which excludes certain items like foreign cash, was 2.9x, well within covenant levels. Capital expenditures were $3.2 million through the first half of the year. We have refined our full year 2025 capital expenditures outlook to a range of $8 million to $10 million compared with the prior estimate of $10 million to $12 million.
Overall, we are executing well across all 3 of our financial priorities for 2025, improving inventory turns and working capital, maintaining cost discipline and reducing debt. These efforts position us well to continue expanding profitability and create financial flexibility for strategic execution.
With that, if you advance to Slide 12, I will now turn the call back over to Dick.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Thank you, Jim. While our book-to-bill ratio was modestly below 1 at 0.97, demand trends remain steady in key sectors like industrial, where our power quality solutions continue to perform well and in aerospace and defense, where we are seeing continued traction with both legacy and new programs.
Backlog ended the quarter at $236.6 million, down slightly from Q1 and prior year levels as customers continue to manage through inventory normalization. The majority of our backlog is still expected to convert within 3 to 9 months, which is consistent with historical patterns.
Importantly, we are seeing signs that the destocking cycle is largely behind us, especially in the industrial automation end markets. Order activity is becoming more consistent and quoting volumes are improving in several key verticals, which gives us confidence heading into the second half. That said, we do expect third quarter sales to be sequentially lower due to the $3 million to $4 million in revenue that was pulled into Q2.
While Europe is showing signs of stabilization, the region has not fully recovered and Q3 is typically a seasonally weaker period in Europe. As we look ahead, our strategy remains unchanged to drive sustainable, profitable growth while delivering lasting value to our customers, employees and shareholders. We continue to align the business around margin-accretive technology-forward solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers in motion, control and power.
The benefits of our Simplify to Accelerate NOW program are clearly reflected in our performance through margin expansion, operating leverage, improved working capital and stronger cash flow. We remain proactive in managing external risks, including tariffs and rare earth supply dynamics. Our mitigation strategies are proving effective, and we are confident in our ability to protect both supply continuity and profitability.
More broadly, we are encouraged by constructive signs across our served markets, supported by long-term trends in electrification, automation, energy efficiency and precision control. This includes seeing early signs of recovery in industrial automation and steady momentum in A&D.
The operational foundation we have built, the strength of our balance sheet and the momentum behind our core initiatives positions us well to execute through the second half and to drive long-term value well beyond.
With that, operator, let's open the line for questions.

Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC
Congrats on the results. So I just want to maybe understand, again, kind of what you're seeing out there. So it sounds like you're feeling good that the destocking is in the rearview mirror. You're starting to maybe see some green shoots in industrial, A&D remains strong. Anything else you want to maybe call out or highlight?

Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.

Gregory William Palm

And I do believe that our team is well positioned to capitalize on it as we move forward. So there will be some minor bumps along the way, but we feel we're on track, and we're in a good position to capitalize on those as they move forward.
Gregory William Palm
Analyst, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC
Okay. Great. And then maybe lastly, on the rare earth magnets, which I know we talked about a lot last quarter. I mean, on a relative basis, given what's happened in the last month, are you feeling better, worse, the same? What's the risk profile there?
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Yes. Our team has worked extremely hard to stay on top of it and engage all of our operations. And I think we have a pretty good outlook what we feel is going to happen. We've seen some improvements, although I just -- we have to be very cautious here and say that this is -- most of the materials that we're talking about are coming out of China, and there's always a risk that things can change in the short-term. But we're starting to see some things loosen up some of the licenses being approved. We still have some exposure.
We talked before about the exposure we see potentially for the remainder of the year, there's somewhere between [ 1 million and 3 million ] in shipments that could be impacted by it. But I would also say to you with -- because of that, I mentioned that we had an accelerated -- some accelerated shipments or pull-ins into Q2. We believe that, that was a reflection of the concern on the heavy rare earth and that our customers wanted to get some supply on hand to make sure that they were protected.
So those were pull aheads. And as it was mentioned that, that could have an impact on our third quarter shipments I also would state that there's no -- we don't have enough visibility. We don't really know what all of our customers' plans are. So while we're saying there could be an impact, we're also knowing -- we're also realizing that they could also pull ahead again. And as long as we had materials to supply that.
And so we emphasize that Q2 was a little higher than what we would have expected based upon the pull aheads and that Q3 could be impacted because of that. But I would also say to you that we are not 100% sure how our customers are going to react and what they're going to do going forward here, if that's just going to be inventory they're going to hold on hand and just continue the supply on a normalized basis with some safety stock in their possession.
So those are things that we're seeing, and that's caused some of that. And I think we are encouraged that there are some positive signs ahead things are loosening up and starting to get to a more normal state.

The next question is from Ted Jackson with Northland Securities.
Edward Randolph Jackson
Research Analyst, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division
Congratulations on a very nice quarter. I've got a few questions. Going back into the pull forward of revenue, just out of curiosity, within your reported segments, where was most of that pull forward coming from segments like Industrial, Medical, Vehicle, et cetera?
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Yes. It's 2 areas that we saw in medical, and what I'll -- it's related around the types of materials that are typically used in the high-performance solutions. So when we talk about heavy rare earth, that usually means higher performance solutions and higher performance comes from, let's say, when we look at from a motor perspective, smaller size but higher energy magnets to produce more power. So I would tell you, medical, some high-end industrial and some defense.
Now also what I would like to state, and I stated this before, Tim, but just allow me to repeat this. Our company has taken an approach more than 10 years ago. As I said before, we go through these cycles. It seems like every 7 to 8 years where magnet prices are under pressure and they get increased 300% to 400% and you have to work with your customers to get enough material to supply their demand and pass along surcharges based upon those prices.
In this case, we were challenged by the fact that we weren't even going to be allowed to receive the material. So that became a little bit more stressful for us. Because of this, what's occurred in the past, our company has been very proactive and designing products where possible that don't contain heavy rare earth. And we will continue to do so into the future to try to eliminate this risk as much as we possibly can off into the future. But we have already and have been for years taking actions to do that, and we have been successful.
Edward Randolph Jackson
Research Analyst, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division
Well, that would be great. And then the fact of the matter is as these barriers to trade come in place, it's driving the development of the domestic market, which over the longer-term would probably be quite [ big. ] So we'll see how it plays out over the next decade or so.
On the magnet supply, I mean, I know as all this came in place that you guys were on top of it and smart and did bring in some heavy earth high-end products into inventory to be in front of it. When you look at where you are with that, I mean, at what point would it become an issue if God forbid, the Chinese just stopped things again. I mean do you have enough supply to get you through the remainder of this year? I mean do you have supply that will take you into '26. And I'm not saying that you're going to run out of it. I'm just saying just kind of understanding like what level of safety stock you put in place.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Well, it varies, and it's -- there's multiple ways that we would be dealing with that. I'm going to let Jim talk a little bit about some of the things that we've done on the supply chain side and the actions that we've taken to ensure that we have material. But I say it varies because if, in fact, you have noticed that you're just not going to receive, and for example, the Chinese will not ship magnets or heavy rare earth materials to the U.S. for defense applications. U.S. doesn't want them, and China won't ship them.
So that's been out there for a while, and it's opened up opportunities domestically, but what that will do is drive pricing and cost will go up. So there's -- the government has taken some actions to mitigate it in the future, and we are on board and in the loop with what's happening here.
So it's just -- it's hard to give you a specific time frame because it will vary based upon products, the amount of safety stock we have for each, what the supply chain is looking like, our resourcing and also identifying some redesign opportunities that worse comes to worse, if you can't get product, then what are the alternatives from a design perspective that we can accelerate through and get approval from customers.
Typically, once our products get designed into these types of applications, the redesign and approval process is a very long period of time. Just like we saw during COVID, though, some of those roadblocks are removed because you had no choice but to remove and to accelerate the process itself.
So if that occurs, then we may be into that and our engineering team rather than focusing on new opportunities and developing opportunities may be redeployed to work on sustaining and corrective actions. But like as I said, we're in the loop on everything that's occurring. There are some good developments, they're going to take time to come online. And maybe, Jim, you want to talk about some of those a bit.
James A. Michaud
Senior VP & Chief Financial Officer
Yes. I mean I think you saw an example of that in yesterday's news where Apple announced that they're making an investment in manufacturing here in the U.S. and part of it had to do with the fact that the government is investing in putting in infrastructure related to our own exploration in rare earth materials and so forth.
So I think we're very encouraged by that. We've been in discussions with a lot of suppliers and as many are, understanding who's going to be a player, who's going to be able to produce and when. So I think we're well in tune with that. And I'm actually very encouraged that some of those opportunities are going to come online sooner than I think any of us expected. And hopefully, we'll participate in that.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
You may want to mention you went to Washington and talk to the government officials.
James A. Michaud
Senior VP & Chief Financial Officer
Yes. I did have an opportunity to go to the Department of Commerce and met with several of the individuals involved in trade talks and so forth and very, very informative. And as I mentioned, they are obviously helping many companies, not dissimilar to ours in identifying opportunities to look at alternate sources and where those are and the like. So there's a great collaboration, I would tell you, between companies and the Department of Commerce to ensure that companies like ours are being supported, and we understand what the alternatives are.
Edward Randolph Jackson
Research Analyst, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division
Great. I have 2 more questions. A quick one, hopefully, in terms of an answer. Just maybe there's nothing even there, but it's just -- it's a hot topic right now. I'm just kind of curious, and then I have one more after that.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
I'll answer it very quickly. It's a hot topic for us as well.
Edward Randolph Jackson
Research Analyst, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division
So you guys are...
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
You said short. You wanted a quick answer, I gave you a quick answer. Yes, we see it as you do. There's definitely some opportunities, and we're well positioned to capitalize on some of this. And without getting into a lot of detail on it for competitive reasons, I mean, it is something that's on our radar.
Edward Randolph Jackson
Research Analyst, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division
Okay. I'll leave it there. And then my last question is, as you -- all your efficiency stuff is coming to roost, you're really doing a good job of driving margins, putting that in the -- making the business stand up and deliver cash and deliver return to shareholders. You're deleveraging the business. You've gotten your business down to for lack of a better term, let's call it, targeted leverage ratios.
Historically, you've always been acquisitive in terms of just building growth through acquisition. As you're kind of exiting some of these strategic efforts in terms of realignment of the business, restructuring the business, making the business more efficient, getting debt paid down. What's going on, on the M&A strategy for you all? How active are you in the pipeline? Are you going to turn it back on? That's my last question.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Yes. We really -- from an investigation, from a grooming standpoint, from identifying opportunities for us in the marketplace, we never shut it down entirely. But what we did do is say it is a time period when we will be establishing communications with certain key opportunities for us in the future that we saw it was a really good strategic fit. It's worked its way into the deep bowels and roots of the company. It's not going to change. We're going to keep doing that. It really is healthy, and it aligns very well with our AST initiatives. So our lean toolkit and training and so forth.
So I would say to you that, yes, we are getting well positioned that we could execute an acquisition. And we will certainly be very cautious and careful to make sure everything is lining up properly that it's a great strategic fit and provide some continued increased value for what we're doing. And that the value of our recent acquisitions have been in -- as we mentioned, has been in certain technologies and market penetration that we were looking for as well as accretive to our average gross margin.

[Operator Instructions] The next question comes from [ Craig Cosgrove, ] private investor.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Mr. Cosgrove used to be a controller for us in one of our operations. I'm guessing maybe by mistake. He's followed us very closely and has been a strong supporter since he's left. So maybe he hit the button by mistake.

And just part B and C on that question, if I may.
Richard S. Warzala

Orin Zvi Hirschman
CEO, AIGH Investment Partners
Did you see some of that already in this past quarter?

Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
We saw an improvement. So we've seen gradual improvement sequentially in Q1 over Q2. So we did see improvement, but we're continuing to see more improvement as we move ahead to get us to the point of normalization. So yes, a little bit, but we expect more coming forward.
Orin Zvi Hirschman

Okay. My last question, which I think someone else alluded to, just on the munition side, there have been a number of companies that have indicated that they're capacity constrained. Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
No. We mentioned the restructuring that we did to consolidate some operations several years ago, I'd say, 3, 4 years ago, we -- the main operation for munitions -- well, there's 2 main operations for us for munitions applications, and those are being consolidated together. But we decided to increase our size of our facility and to allow us to grow into it. And that has put us in a really good position to -- to answer your question, we are not capacity constrained.
Orin Zvi Hirschman
CEO, AIGH Investment Partners
Okay. Are you seeing the same as other vendors in terms of the desire from your...
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
What we've seen -- yes. So what we've seen, there's -- certainly in the supply chain side of it, there can be some concern, but we haven't -- we've been working on sourcing for a while here when you go back to when the conflicts broke out and then the initial inquiries on what the projected demand might be. And over time, I don't -- Orin, I'm not sure that you had invested in us yet, but we had talked about that, that the inquiry level was quite high, but we hadn't seen any POs from that to increase the capacity.
We not have seen that. We have seen the orders come to fruition, and we now are beginning to ship at higher levels. And so we were prepared. We went out and we did quite a bit of work in advance of this because we were getting quotation requests for some significantly higher volumes. So we were preparing our supply base as well as preparing ourselves, and that is coming to fruition.
Operator
This concludes our question-and-answer session. I would now like to turn the call back to management for closing remarks.
Richard S. Warzala
Chairman, CEO & President, Allied Motion Technologies Inc.
Thank you, everyone, for joining us on today's call and for your interest in Allient. As always, please feel free to reach out to us at any time, and we look forward to talking to you all again after our third quarter 2025 results. Have a great day.
Operator
The conference has now concluded. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect your lines.

The process has been productive, yielding a pool of high caliber candidates, and we anticipate welcoming an external candidate on-board very soon. Given the timing, Mike graciously agreed to extend his tenure as CFO into the end of June, which will facilitate a smooth transition of his duties. Due to prior planned commitments, Mike couldn't join us on today's call, and Jackson Trostle will be filling in for him. I would like to take this moment to extend my heartfelt wishes to Mike as he embarks on his retirement. Throughout his tenure, Mike has been an outstanding partner and has played a key role in establishing the framework necessary for us to support the levels of growth we've achieved over the years. Under his leadership, he has also cultivated a strong supporting team, laying a solid foundation for our continued success in the future.
I would also like to express gratitude to two other individuals for their guidance and support over the years. Jim Tanous, our Director since 2014, has chosen not to stand for re-election, resulting in a reduction of our board size to 6 members after yesterday's annual meeting.
